title: Causal-tree analysis & automated safety adoption for failed staged deploy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up work from the March 2 staged deployment that resulted in a partial rollback. This ticket captures the causal-tree reconstruction we ran across telemetry signals, the gaps found in the existing safety checklist, and a concrete plan to adopt automated safety gates (hysteresis + guard rails) into the staged deploy pipeline. The goal is: 1) codify the failure modes and detectable precursors, 2) extend the runbook to make automated safe-abort decisions, and 3) land a minimal set of observability + KV-cache tagging changes that prevent this class of false-positives/false-negatives in future canaries.
postmortem_summary: Root causes: (a) KV-cache keyspace collision between two model variants caused mismatch in cached prefixes for shadow traffic, (b) metric drift (response-token-distribution KL divergence) exceeded subjective threshold but was not correlated with user-facing latency metrics, and (c) hysteresis values in the rollback automation were too aggressive given workload burstiness. Contributing factors: incomplete telemetry contract between shadow harness and canary scoring service; missing tag propagation for cache namespace. Impact: 4% of canary traffic experienced higher sampling token mismatch and 2% increased p95 latency for a 45-minute window. No customer data leaked, but degraded responses observed for internal QA flows.
decision_log: 2026-03-06 — Decision: Build a causal-tree reconstruction pipeline to correlate KV-cache events, token-distribution drift, and latency spikes rather than treating each signal independently. Owner: Liam Chen
2026-03-07 — Decision: Add cache-namespace tagging to outgoing model requests from shadow mode to avoid keyspace collision. Owner: Marina Kovacs

2026-03-08 — Decision: Replace the current single-threshold canary abort with a two-stage hysteresis: fast abort on hard SLO breaches (latency error budget) and soft stall on distributional drift until confirmatory signals arrive. Owner: Aisha Patel
2026-03-09 — Decision: Require a lightweight security and compliance checklist for automated abort rules (no PII in signals). Owner: Rajesh Bhatia
